newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries steady in sluggish Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries steady in sluggish Tokyo.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were little changed by Tokyo midday on Thursday with their tone slightly weak following slight falls overnight, traders said.
Light trading was detected in the 10-year sector, but otherwise a wait-and-see mood dominated amid a lack of fresh trading incentives, they said.
"Operators were unwilling to build up fresh positions. The market is thin as some operators are already on summer vacations," a trader at a U.S. brokerage said.
The 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond was at 102-18/32, yielding 6.43 percent, compared with 102-16/32 in New York.

Traders said underlying sentiment remained bullish. They said operators were eager to test prices up further as credit-tightening concerns had faded after remarks by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan reduced concerns about U.S. inflation.

"Given this sentiment, I won't be very surprised to see the yield (of the 30-year bond) dip to 6.30 percent. The market may also test the 10-year note yield below the 6.0 percent threshold," the trader said.
In Wednesday's New York trading, prices closed slightly lower as players took some profits while digesting new remarks by several top Federal Reserve officials and a government debt auction.

In the short-term, dealers expect prices to maintain their bullish trend, with the market looking towards the U.S. employment cost index (ECI) for the second quarter due to be released on Tuesday, and jobs data on August 1.
"With Humphrey-Hawkins testimony and auctions out of the way, the market is expected to stay quiet until the ECI data," another trader said.
The September T-bond futures contract was down 4/32 at 115-9/32 by 0340 GMT. It moved in a range of 115-5/32 to 115-12/32 in Tokyo trading time.
